newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says southern rebel commander defects.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says southern rebel commander defects.

text.p: Sudan said on Sunday a commander with the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) had left the group and asked for peace with the government.
The official news agency SUNA said Major Nikrona Magar Ashiek, a commander in the Lakes and Upper Nile areas in southern Sudan, had defected but did not say when.
Federal Rule Chamber Minister Ali al-Haj Mohammad said Ashiek's defection was "a big gain for the peace march in the country", SUNA reported.
The agency said Ashiek was a former communications minister in the SPLA, which is led by John Garang.

"It is important that Commander Ashiek has joined the peace process as he was one of the leading commanders of Garang's movement and Garang's assistant for military operations particularly in Western Equatoria," Mohammad said.
SUNA quoted Ashiek as saying the SPLA had adopted false methods and was without goals.
"The movement is no longer able to liberate the south, let alone claim the liberation of the whole of Sudan," SUNA quoted Ashiek as saying.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north.
